task: Identify the upgrade options available for the cheapest base model of the MacBook Pro 14-inch with M5 chip, and calculate the total price difference from the base model to the maximum upgrade (no Pre-Installed Software) offered by Apple.
answer:
FINAL: The original US$1,599 base 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 could be upgraded to US$3,369 without pre-installed software—a total increase of US$1,770.

The base configuration has a 10-core CPU/10-core GPU M5, 16GB unified memory, 512GB SSD, standard display and 70W USB-C adapter.

Hardware upgrade options and additional prices from that base:
- Memory: 24GB +$200; 32GB +$400.
- Storage: 1TB +$200; 2TB +$600; 4TB +$1,200.
- Nano-texture display: +$150.
- 96W USB-C adapter: +$20.

Maximum M5 configuration: 32GB memory, 4TB SSD, nano-texture display and 96W adapter. Calculation: $400 + $1,200 + $150 + $20 = $1,770; $1,599 + $1,770 = $3,369. Prices exclude tax, software and AppleCare.

Evidence:
- Apple’s October 15, 2025 announcement gives the original $1,599 US starting price: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2025/10/apple-unveils-new-14-inch-macbook-pro-powered-by-the-m5-chip/
- Apple’s M5 specifications list the available hardware upgrades: https://support.apple.com/en-us/125405
- AppleInsider’s Pricing section gives the upgrade charges and explicitly states the $3,369 maximum. Screenshot: final.png. https://appleinsider.com/inside/macbook-pro/vs/m5-macbook-pro-vs-m4-macbook-pro-incremental-but-welcome-upgrade

Checked October 27, 2026. These are the original M5 prices. Apple’s live US configurator now lists M6, M5 Pro and M5 Max and redirects ordinary M5 configuration links, so a current M5 order total could not be obtained: https://www.apple.com/shop/buy-mac/macbook-pro
